title: Runbook
description: A cached, replayable procedure. Produced by hand (M1) or distilled from a winning trajectory (M3), executed by RunbookExecutor. RECONCILED at H+1: the action/arguments model comes from the shipped implementation in src/runbook_voice/runbooks.py, which this schema documents rather than competes with. Keep the two in step - if you change one, change the other.

version.description: String, not integer - Runbook.from_dict coerces with str().

description.description: What this runbook does, in one sentence. The semantic matcher searches against this, so describe the TASK, not the implementation.

utterance_examples.description: Phrasings that should match. Also the source of truth for the rehearsal script - a presenter improvising a phrasing the matcher never saw is how demos die.

slots.description: Values supplied at replay time. The dialogue layer asks for missing ones in declaration order.

steps.description: Dispatched in order to the persistent runner. Stop on first failure - no implicit retries.

prompt.description: GRAFTED AT RECONCILIATION. Spoken aloud when this slot is unfilled, so it must be a question a person would actually ask - 'How many people?' not 'the party size'. The shipped model's `description` is documentation and is not askable.

type.description: Mirrors SlotType. A step argument that is exactly {{slot}} preserves this type; embedded in a larger string it becomes text.

action.description: Namespaced verb dispatched to the runner, e.g. restaurant.search. Deliberately abstract: no URLs, no CSS selectors. Selectors baked into a runbook break the first time the provider ships a redesign, and a synthesized runbook full of them would be unmaintainable.

arguments.description: Passed to the runner after {{slot}} substitution. Substitution is recursive through nested objects and arrays.

irreversible.description: INVARIANT 1. True for anything with an out-of-box side effect: bookings, charges, sent messages. The executor routes these through the confirmation gate, and branches must never run them.

confirmation_prompt.description: Spoken readback before an irreversible step. Supports {{slot}} templating - the executor substitutes before handing it to the gate, and an unresolvable reference fails closed. Must name specifics (what, when, how many); 'shall I proceed?' is not acceptable.

then.$comment: GRAFTED AT RECONCILIATION. Structural, not advisory: a runbook that books without a spoken gate is invalid rather than a code-review catch. The executor already fails closed when the gate is missing; this closes the same hole at the document level.
